data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small, independently operated services is more resilient to correlated failure than a large, redundant service because it replaces 'redundancy of component' with 'diversity of operational plane'.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services all rely on a single, common upstream dependency (e.g., a specific cloud provider's regional API).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'diversity' is superficial, and all services utilize the same underlying vulnerable library or framework (ref: SCR_004).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a large service, internal redundancy (e.g., 100x replicas) typically shares a unified control plane, deployment pipeline, or configuration schema. A single 'poison pill' update or global state corruption (as noted in SRC_005) propagates across all redundant units simultaneously. A decentralized network utilizes diverse operational planes (different OS, languages, and human operators), ensuring that a failure in one operational paradigm does not logically map to another, thereby capping the blast radius of any single systemic error (ref: SCR_002).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
